prompt:
Draw the land borders and coastline of Poland as of 1 January 1938 from memory.

Rules:
- Draw land only. Each separate piece of territory (mainland, island, exclave) is its own polygon. Do not enclose sea.
- Leave out overseas dependencies and Antarctic claims.
- Use at most 400 points in total.
- Your drawing is scored by overlap: the area it shares with the true territory, divided by the total area covered by either. Missing land and extra land both cost you.
- Give your best attempt even if you are unsure. An approximate drawing is expected.

Format:
- You may reason first. End with one ```geojson block; only that block is scored.
- The block holds a single GeoJSON MultiPolygon:
  {"type": "MultiPolygon", "coordinates": [[[[lon, lat], [lon, lat], ...]], [[[lon, lat], ...]]]}
- Longitude first, then latitude, in decimal degrees with at most 2 decimal places. West and south are negative.

I'll draw Poland's borders as of January 1, 1938. At this time, Poland had its interwar borders established by the Treaty of Versailles and subsequent agreements. Key features:

- Western border with Germany (including the Polish Corridor giving access to the Baltic Sea)
- Northern coast along the Baltic Sea (including Gdańsk corridor)
- Eastern borders with Lithuania, Soviet Union (USSR)
- Southern borders with Romania, Czechoslovakia
- The Free City of Danzig was separate but Poland had the corridor

Let me think about the approximate coordinates:

- Poland in 1938 was larger than modern Poland, extending further east (into what is now Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania)
- Western border was roughly similar to today
- Eastern border went much further east - roughly to Vilnius area in north, Lwów (Lviv) area in south-east

Key points to remember:
- Western border around 14-19°E
- Eastern border around 24-27°E (much further east than today)
- North coast around 54.5-55°N
- South border around 49-49.5°N

The Polish Corridor ran between Germany and East Prussia, giving access to Baltic Sea at roughly 18-19°E.
